tone: friendly-professional, second-person, conversational. No exclamation marks. No emoji. Avoid marketing-speak inflation.
formality: Polite (สุภาพ). Use formal vocabulary but keep sentence length natural and readable. Avoid the spoken particles ครับ/ค่ะ except where directly addressing the reader as a CTA. Do not over-translate Anglicisms that Thai golfers use natively (กรีน, แฟร์เวย์, สวิง are familiar Thai golf terms — keep them rather than forcing pure Thai equivalents).
preserve: All numerals (do not translate to Thai numerals)

currency.note: RULING: Thai prose spells the currency as บาท (108 uses vs 0 'THB' in messages/th.json). The ฿ symbol appears occasionally as source data (preserve where present); do not introduce the Latin 'THB' abbreviation into Thai prose.

style_notes: Polite (สุภาพ) register; avoid spoken particles ครับ/ค่ะ except in direct CTA address.
Keep familiar English-derived golf terms (กรีน, แฟร์เวย์, สวิง, พาร์, เบอร์ดี้) rather than pure-Thai coinages.
Arabic digits with a space before spelled units (1,800 บาท); no exclamation marks, no emoji.

No em dash (— or ——) anywhere in copy, titles included, per the owner's house style, and no look-alike used as a separator in its place (–, ―, ─, a spaced hyphen). This glossary has no seo_norms, so for a title use the separators docs/i18n-review-checklist.md names under SERP / SEO checks. In body copy, replace the dash by what it was doing. Between two clauses use a space, Thai's own clause and sentence break; when the second clause explains or follows from the first, a connective (คือ, ซึ่ง, จึง, เพราะ) often reads better than a bare space. Do not reach for a comma: Thai prose rarely puts one between clauses. For an aside or gloss use half-width parentheses () with a space before the opening and after the closing parenthesis (กระทรวงการต่างประเทศ (mfa.go.th) และ …). Before an explanation or a list of examples use a colon followed by one space. A bold label or lead-in takes the colon inside the bold rather than a dash after it (**ค่าแคดดี้:** 300-500 บาท), and so does a list item's lead word (2. ไดรฟ์ไกลที่สุด: วัดผล…). Hyphen for ranges only (300-500 บาท), never as a separator. One exception: the ' — ' venue delimiter inside price_breakdown[].item in data/price-guide-pages.ts is a code separator (PriceGuidePage.groupPriceRows() splits on it), so keep it byte-for-byte as ' — ' (half-width space, one —, half-width space; never ——, a colon, a hyphen or a dash without its spaces) exactly where the EN entry has one, and add none elsewhere. Shipped TH copy still contains em dashes: that is legacy debt for a separate native-QA sweep, not a pattern to copy.
